key_insight: A two-stage rule-based + LLM screening pipeline showed very strong agreement with human reviewers for automatic exclusion in a medical systematic review.
clinical_relevance: This suggests AI could safely reduce reviewer workload in title-abstract screening, especially for the large low-priority majority of records.
method: 904 screened records were split into INCLUDE, EXCLUDE, and UNCERTAIN; 185 were stratified for validation.
Three independent physicians reviewed the sample blind to the automated labels.
Agreement was assessed with PABAK, Gwet’s AC1, sensitivity, specificity, WSS, and NNR.
evidence_signal: For the primary automatic-exclusion target, agreement was perfect versus two reviewers and near-perfect versus the third, with 670/904 records (74.1%) in the EXCLUDE stratum.
watch_item: Results come from one review topic and a stratified validation sample, so generalization to other topics, reviewers, or prompting setups remains uncertain.
paper_title: Validation of a two-stage automated screening pipeline for medical systematic reviews: a stratified concordance study with three independent human reviewers, using PABAK and Gwet's AC1
